tailMarker.note: Earliest tail-class species is PARFUM @7. The declared allergens (LINALOOL @17, LIMONENE @18, BENZYL SALICYLATE @20) and the preservatives (BENZOIC ACID @16, BENZYL ALCOHOL @19) all follow it, so the class order is consistent and this is not the 'Parfum at the end behind its allergens' convention. The base (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @5, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6) outranks the marker. Coconut oil @10 and the guar polymer @12 sit in the tail as secondary species. CAPRYLYL GLYCOL @13 (a booster) sits above BENZOIC ACID @16, but both are below the marker, where order is arbitrary; that does not touch the marker species. tail_index-1 = GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6.

conditioning_level.rationale: S2 fires (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2). S3 fires (ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, R4a, plus GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6). S1 fails, because STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @5 is the only cationic surfactant above the tail. S2+S3 without S1 is moderate (R3). The boundary oil is not load-bearing for the value, which would still be moderate on S2 alone.
evidenceSignals: S3 ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4 + GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6
counterSignals: single cationic surfactant on the whole list
Macadamia @8, sunflower @9, coconut @10, coco-caprylate @11 are tail (no credit)

weight_potential.rationale: Heavy-lipid core: GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6 is above PARFUM @7. It is read as R4b because the standard's R4b examples include olive and argan, and the lexicon puts both in the same conventional plant-triglyceride band as soy. Completer: CETEARYL ALCOHOL is a cetearyl-class alcohol in the top three ranks. No lightness positioning conflicts. The value hinges on the tail_index-1 oil (E1), so confidence is capped at moderate. Without the oil all three leanness conjuncts hold (no R4b above the marker, no silicone, SAPDMA the only cationic on the full list), so the value would be low.
counterSignals: the whole high call rests on one species at tail_index-1 whose R4b band is itself a mapping question (lexicon 'mid' band)
without it the formula would satisfy the low leanness test

care_direction.rationale: No R5 protein, peptide or keratin species appears anywhere on the list. The care result comes from a coherent cetearyl/amidoamine/emollient base (IPM @4, soy oil @6), which is the moisture default. Reading (b) is impossible: there is no film or acid route above the tail and an R4 stack is present. The marker is plausible and there is no protein payload, no tail cluster and no competing leg.
evidenceSignals: emollient base IPM @4, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6

repair_support_level.rationale: No R5 route and no named bond token appear anywhere, so only ordinary conditioning and lubrication remain. The INCI is verified and the marker plausible.
evidenceSignals: no R5 / R7 species on the list

primary_focus.rationale: Repair, curl and colour have no route. Moisture fails criterion 1 (only GLYCERIN @3 is above the tail; CAPRYLYL GLYCOL @13 is a tail booster). Shine fails criterion 1: there is no above-tail silicone or polymer and an R4b lipid is present. Smoothing would only reuse the rich R1+R4 base, which §6 rule 1 counts as one M1 observation, and detangling has no distinctive slip route. The verdict is nonspecific, which resolves to general. Claim role is not_applicable.
counterSignals: competing smoothing rejected: baseline M1 lipid/fatty base only

secondary_focus.rationale: No route clears its own threshold. The single-glycerin humectant leg is not a cluster, so the E10 moisture secondary is unavailable.
